title: AWS ACE: A Practical Co-Sell Guide for ISVs
summary: AWS ACE explained for ISV sellers: how APN Customer Engagements power co-sell, how to share opportunities, sync from your CRM, and unlock partner funding.
body_text: AWS ACE (APN Customer Engagements) is the program and system ISVs use to co-sell with AWS — sharing sales opportunities and leads with AWS field teams so both sides work the same deal toward a marketplace close. For an independent software vendor (ISV) selling on AWS, the fastest path to a bigger deal is rarely a better cold email. It’s an AWS account executive who already has the customer’s trust and a number to hit. Co-sell is how you get in that room. The mechanism has a bureaucratic name — APN Customer Engagements, or ACE — and a reputation for living inside a portal nobody enjoys. But the payoff is real: shared pipeline, AWS field alignment, and funding that direct selling never unlocks. Here’s how ACE works, and how to run it without your alliances team living in Partner Central. What is AWS ACE? AWS ACE (APN Customer Engagements) is the co-sell system inside AWS Partner Central where partners and AWS share opportunities and leads. A partner submits a deal it’s working; AWS validates and routes it to the right field team; and from there both sides collaborate toward a close — usually a transaction on AWS Marketplace . ACE is the operational layer of the AWS Partner Network (APN). Membership gets you in the door; ACE is where the actual co-selling happens, deal by deal — a shared pipeline between your company and AWS, with a validation step in the middle that keeps both sides honest about who’s really engaged. An opportunity is a deal you’re already working and want AWS to help close; a lead is a prospect surfaced to you that you can choose to pursue. Most ISV co-sell value comes from opportunities. How opportunity and lead sharing works Co-sell through ACE follows a consistent loop. You submit an opportunity, AWS validates it, and both sides work it once it’s accepted. Submit. You share an opportunity with AWS — customer, use case, deal stage, expected value, and what you need from the AWS team. AWS validates. An AWS reviewer checks the opportunity for completeness and legitimacy, then accepts or returns it for more detail. Route and align. Accepted opportunities are routed to the relevant AWS account team, who can now see the deal alongside their own account plan. Co-sell. Both sides collaborate — introductions, technical validation, next steps — and update status as the deal moves. Close. The deal transacts, increasingly as an AWS Marketplace private offer, and the co-sell record reflects the outcome. The validation step is the part ISVs underestimate. A thin, half-filled opportunity gets returned or ignored; a complete one gets an AWS seller’s attention. Quality of submission is the single biggest lever on whether co-sell works for you. Eligibility: who can co-sell through ACE To co-sell through ACE you need to be an APN member in good standing, with your organization’s AWS Partner Central account set up for co-sell. Beyond membership, the practical gate is opportunity quality — AWS validates each engagement, so a well-formed opportunity is what actually moves. Progress in APN — reaching validated partner stages and earning relevant competencies — expands what you can do: more field engagement, better funding access, stronger co-sell standing. The requirements shift over time, so treat AWS’s current Partner Central documentation as the source of truth. The point for an ISV: co-sell eligibility isn’t a one-time checkbox. It grows with your APN investment, and the partners who put in that work get more from the AWS field. Why co-sell and marketplace work together Co-sell and marketplace are two halves of one motion, not separate programs. Co-sell aligns the AWS field team behind your deal; AWS Marketplace is where that deal actually transacts. The ACE opportunity gets the AWS seller engaged, and a private offer closes the co-sold deal. This matters because a marketplace transaction can count toward the customer’s committed AWS spend — a strong reason for the buyer to say yes, and for the AWS account team to help. When your co-sell record and your marketplace transaction are the same deal seen from two angles, the field has every incentive to push it over the line. If you’re new to the selling side of that transaction, our AWS Marketplace for sellers guide covers listings and private offers end to end. The manual-entry problem — and how CRM-to-ACE sync fixes it The most common way co-sell fails isn’t strategy. It’s data entry. Your deals live in Salesforce or HubSpot; ACE lives in Partner Central; and keeping the two in sync means an alliances manager re-typing opportunities into a portal, then re-typing status back into the CRM. That double entry is where opportunities quietly stop getting submitted. Manual Partner Central entry CRM-to-ACE sync Where deals originate Re-typed by hand into the portal Flow from the CRM your reps already use Status updates Two systems, updated separately One update, reflected on both sides What gets submitted Whatever someone had time to enter Every qualifying opportunity Syncing your CRM to ACE removes the copy-paste tax. Opportunities originate where your reps already work, submissions happen automatically, and AWS field updates flow back without anyone living in the portal. This is exactly the friction Suger’s co-sell automation removes for alliances and partnerships teams — across all three hyperscalers, not just AWS. Partner funding programs AWS offers funding programs that help partners de-risk co-sold deals — support for proof-of-concept work, migration, and marketing-development-style activity that moves a specific opportunity forward. The programs and their requirements change, and eligibility often ties back to your APN stage and the strength of the underlying opportunity. The practical takeaway: funding follows well-run co-sell, not the other way around. A clean, validated ACE opportunity with an engaged AWS account team is the context in which funding requests get approved. Check AWS’s current program documentation for what’s available to your partner tier — and treat a disciplined co-sell process as the prerequisite. Frequently asked questions What is AWS ACE? AWS ACE (APN Customer Engagements) is the co-sell system in AWS Partner Central where partners and AWS share sales opportunities and leads. Partners submit deals, AWS validates them, and both sides collaborate toward a close — usually an AWS Marketplace transaction. What’s the difference between an opportunity and a lead in ACE? An opportunity is a deal you’re already working and want AWS to help close. A lead is a prospect surfaced to you that you can choose to pursue. Most ISV co-sell value comes from sharing opportunities you already own. Do I need to be an APN member to use ACE? Yes. ACE co-sell requires APN membership in good standing and a Partner Central account configured for co-sell. Reaching validated partner stages and earning competencies expands your field engagement and funding access over time. How does ACE relate to AWS Marketplace? They’re two halves of one motion. ACE aligns the AWS field team behind your deal; AWS Marketplace is where it transacts, often as a private offer. The co-sell record and the marketplace transaction are the same deal seen from two sides. Why do co-sell opportunities get missed? Usually manual entry. Deals live in your CRM, ACE lives in Partner Central, and re-typing between them means opportunities go unsubmitted. Syncing your CRM to ACE removes the double entry so every qualifying deal reaches AWS. Can I automate co-sell across more than one cloud? Yes. Suger automates co-sell across three hyperscalers — AWS ACE, Microsoft Partner Center, and Google Cloud Partner Advantage — from one system, so alliances teams run the same motion everywhere instead of one portal at a time. Takeaways ACE is the operational layer of APN — membership gets you in, but validated, well-formed opportunities are what actually move the AWS field. Submission quality is the biggest lever. A complete opportunity gets an AWS seller’s attention; a thin one gets returned or ignored. Treat co-sell and marketplace as one deal. The ACE opportunity engages the field; the private offer closes it against committed AWS spend. The most common co-sell failure is data entry. Sync your CRM to ACE so every qualifying opportunity gets submitted without portal work. Suger’s co-sell automation syncs opportunities from Salesforce and HubSpot into AWS ACE — and into Microsoft and Google Cloud co-sell — so your team runs pipeline from the CRM they already use instead of living in Partner Central. See how it fits your alliance motion, and where marketplace close comes next.

title: The Collaboration Gap in Zero Trust: Why Sovereignty Can’t Stop at the Perimeter
summary: The core principle of Zero Trust is simple: don't assume trust based on the network. But many organizations don't apply that idea to collaboration.
body_text: Zero Trust is the defining security framework for defense and government operations. Verify every user. Authenticate every device. Trust nothing by default. But there’s a gap most organizations aren’t talking about: collaboration . While agencies have made significant strides in securing networks, endpoints, and data at rest, the tools their teams use to actually work — to coordinate missions, share intelligence, and make decisions in real time — blend multiple data sources and policies and inconsistently inherit and enforce zero policies. They’re cloud-hosted, vendor-controlled, and built for commercial enterprises with simpler access policies, not classified environments. That gap is a risk. And it’s time to close it. Zero Trust Is a Mindset, Not Just an Architecture The core principle of Zero Trust is simple: don’t assume trust based on the network. But too many organizations apply that principle to infrastructure while leaving collaboration as an afterthought. Think about what happens in a typical operational workflow. Analysts coordinate over messaging tools hosted in commercial clouds. Decision makers share sensitive context through platforms where data retention policies, encryption keys, and access controls belong to the vendor instead of the mission owner. That’s not Zero Trust. That’s a blind spot. The DoD’s Zero Trust Strategy makes this explicit, and defense organizations are now under real pressure to reach Target and Advanced Level Zero Trust across their entire operational stack. That includes the tools teams use to communicate and share files every day. Authentication, authorization, and encryption are critical but usually only control over who can access data, under what conditions, and for how long at an initial point of time. Existing collaboration platforms simply weren’t built to enforce data-centric security continuously as messages flow. True Zero Trust requires that every layer of the operational stack, including how your people talk to each other, meets the same standard. And for defense and intelligence organizations, there’s no getting there without solving for data sovereignty first. Sovereignty Is the New Security Baseline Data sovereignty used to be a nice-to-have. Today, you can’t reach Target and Advanced Level Zero Trust without it. Zero Trust asks who can touch the data, under what conditions, and for how long. Sovereignty asks who controls the infrastructure, keys, and policies that actually answer that question. Skip sovereignty, and you’re trusting someone else’s word instead of enforcing your own control, the exact assumption Zero Trust was designed to remove. For defense and intelligence environments, that shift is underway: moving from network-centric to data-centric security. The difference matters. Network-centric security protects the perimeter. Data-centric security protects the data itself, embedding protection directly so that controls persist wherever the information travels, across users, environments, and classification boundaries. Sovereign collaboration means your organization controls: Where data lives : on your infrastructure, in your environment, under your jurisdiction Who holds the keys : persistent, cryptographic protection managed by you, not a third-party vendor What happens to it : policy-based access controls that follow the file, not just the network How long access lasts : the ability to restrict, revoke, and audit at the data level This is what standards like the Zero Trust Data Format (ZTDF), Allied Communication Publication (ACP) 240, and NIST SP 800-171 are driving toward, and it’s what Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) compliance increasingly demands. The collaboration platform has to work where the mission is — disconnected, deployed, and fully under control. Sovereign AI Changes the Game — But Only If You Control the Foundation AI is reshaping how intelligence workflows operate. With automated summarization, pattern recognition, and decision support, the potential is significant. But AI is only as trustworthy as the environment it runs in. Sovereign AI means running models inside your environment, on your data, with your controls. It means the insights generated by AI never leave the boundary you’ve defined. And it means your teams can actually trust what the AI is telling them because they know where it came from and how it was built. You can’t bolt sovereignty onto an AI model hosted in a commercial cloud. You have to build it into the foundation, starting with the collaboration layer where that data originates. The Operational Collaboration Platform for What’s Next The convergence of Zero Trust, data sovereignty, and sovereign AI is happening now, on the floor at DoDIIS, in procurement conversations, and in the architectures being designed for the next generation of defense operations. The teams getting ahead of it are the ones building on platforms designed for this environment from the start, not commercial tools retrofitted with security add-ons. That means a collaboration layer where sensitive files are protected the moment they’re shared, with controls that persist wherever the data travels. The platform itself acts as the policy enforcement point, with data protection that’s cryptographic, not assumed. Secure collaboration can’t be a chokepoint that comes at the expense of mission speed. And it doesn’t have to be. The right architecture makes security and operational velocity the same thing instead of a trade-off. Collaboration that’s self-hosted, air-gappable, Zero Trust-native, and sovereign by design isn’t a luxury for high-stakes environments. It’s the only option that makes sense. title: AutoRFP vs SiftHub: A Neutral 2026 Comparison
summary: Compare AutoRFP vs SiftHub to see which RFP tool reduces rework, improves response quality, and helps your team submit faster.
body_text: Last reviewed: July 2026. This comparison is based on vendor-published materials, verified G2 and Capterra reviews, and independent third-party analyses. Pricing and feature details change over time, so confirm current specifics directly with each vendor before purchasing. TL;DR AutoRFP.ai fits teams that want transparent, project-based pricing and a structured way to turn RFPs, DDQs, and security questionnaires into drafted responses with confidence scoring, though several reviewers flag its interface as a weak point. SiftHub is best understood as an "AI sales engineer" a broader deal-support platform where RFP response is one module alongside live in-call assistance, meeting prep, and proposals grounded in CRM and call data. Neither is objectively better the right pick depends on whether you are optimizing for RFP throughput or for broader deal support. If your real bottleneck is a messy, contradictory knowledge library, an AI-native alternative like Inventive AI is worth a look before you commit. What Should You Consider When Choosing Between AutoRFP and SiftHub? Before you sit through two demos, decide which of these criteria actually matter to your team. Use the probing question next to each to structure your evaluation: AI drafting capability How much of a first draft does each tool generate on the first pass, and how much editing does that draft need before it is client-ready? Ask for a live run on one of your own documents. Content governance Who controls which sources the AI can draw from, and how are approvals enforced? Ask how the tool prevents an unapproved answer from shipping. Conflict detection When two sources disagree, does the platform flag it, or does it silently pick one? Ask each vendor to demonstrate this on purposely conflicting content. Hallucination control Can the AI generate answers outside your approved library, and how is each answer traced back to a source? Ask to see source citations on every generated response. Narrative-style proposals Beyond filling spreadsheets, can the tool draft prose sections and executive summaries in your voice? Test a narrative-heavy RFP, not just a Q&A grid. Content management How is the knowledge library kept fresh, deduplicated, and current? Ask what maintenance is automated versus manual. Workflow automation Can you route questions to SMEs, track progress, and enforce review stages without leaving the tool? Walk through a multi-reviewer workflow in the demo. Collaboration Do unlimited team members get access, or is collaboration gated by seat count? Confirm how pricing scales with reviewers. Integrations Does it connect to your CRM, content repositories, and communication tools? Confirm the specific connectors you need are live, not on a roadmap. Security and compliance Which certifications does each vendor hold, and where is your data stored? Ask for ISO, SOC 2, and any penetration-test evidence. Analytics Can you see win rates, response times, and content usage? Ask what reporting is available out of the box. Pricing Is pricing published and predictable, or quote-only? Compare total cost including onboarding and library maintenance, and cross-check figures against pages like the Inventive AutoRFP pricing and reviews breakdown and the SiftHub pricing and reviews guide . Ease of implementation How long from signing to a usable library? Ask for a realistic onboarding timeline with a customer reference. Enterprise scalability Does it hold up on 500- to 2,000-question RFPs and across multiple business units? Ask for an enterprise customer story at your scale. AutoRFP vs SiftHub at a Glance ‍ AutoRFP.ai SiftHub Best for Bid and proposal teams that want transparent pricing and fast, structured RFP/DDQ/security-questionnaire responses Sales and presales teams that want an "AI sales engineer" spanning RFPs plus live deal support G2 rating 4.9 / 5 (56 reviews) 4.5 / 5 (22 reviews) AI capabilities AI drafting in company tone with per-answer "Trust Scores" Auto-fills ~90% on first pass across major questionnaire formats, source-traced Response quality Reviewers cite strong time savings; some note editing needed Reviewers cite accurate autofill; some note generic answers needing tweaks Conflict detection Not marketed as a native feature Not marketed as a native feature Content management Centralized content library, browser extension for portals Central hub sifting content across Drive, SharePoint, CRM, knowledge bases Competitive intelligence agents Not a marketed feature Not a marketed feature Collaboration Unlimited users on all plans; SME workflows, progress tracking Shared workspace, SME coordination, governance workflows Integrations 18+ integrations (per vendor) Slack, Salesforce, HubSpot, Drive, SharePoint, OneDrive, Notion, Gong, Zendesk, Teams, Highspot Workflow automation Purpose-built bid workflows, real-time progress tracking Bid/no-bid qualification, SME routing, governance Security ISO 27001:2022, SOC 2 ISO certified, SOC 2 certified, VAPT certified Pricing Published: from $899/mo (Scale) to $1,299/mo (Accelerate); Enterprise custom Custom quote, not publicly published Customer support Unlimited support and onboarding included on all plans Onboarding and support per contract ‍ Note: pricing and rating figures above are reported figures drawn from vendor pages and G2 at the time of writing. Confirm current numbers directly with each vendor. AutoRFP.ai AutoRFP.ai is an AI RFP response platform aimed at sales and bid teams. It positions itself around speed and transparency: turning RFPs, RFIs, DDQs, and security questionnaires into drafted responses quickly, with predictable pricing. Its primary use cases are structured questionnaire response and bid management. AutoRFP.ai best features AI drafting in your voice. The engine analyzes requirements, searches your content, and drafts responses using your company's terminology and tone, per vendor documentation. Trust Scores. Each generated answer carries a confidence indicator tied to the strength of its source content, which reviewers use to prioritize what to check. Multi-format support via browser extension. It handles Excel, Word, PDF, and online portal submissions through a browser extension, which matters for buyers who submit through procurement portals. Purpose-built bid workflows. SME assignment, reviewer stages, and real-time progress tracking are built in, so questions can be routed without leaving the tool. Transparent, project-based pricing. All plans include unlimited users and all features, so collaboration does not inflate the bill per seat. Enterprise security and translation. The platform is ISO 27001:2022 certified and SOC 2 compliant, includes 18+ integrations, and offers translation, per the vendor's pricing page. AutoRFP.ai limitations UI/UX is a recurring complaint: Interface quality is the most consistent knock in reviews: users describe navigation as unintuitive, reordering columns like "Requirement, Response, Compliance, Trust" as awkward, and one reviewer says "some of the UI is a little janky, and the import process can be slightly confusing for the most complex RFPs." Buyers weighing this often read the dedicated Inventive AI vs AutoRFP alternative comparison to see how newer, AI-native interfaces handle the same workflow. ‍ Web-only access. One G2 reviewer notes "Web only access is somewhat limiting," which can constrain teams that want offline or native-app workflows. Initial learning curve. Multiple reviewers mention a learning curve; one writes the "initial learning curve is a little challenging," easing after training. No native CRM or job tracking. A reviewer wishes "there was a CRM of sorts integrated into the software for better job... tracking," so deal tracking still lives elsewhere. Project-based caps. Plans are metered by projects per year (24 on Scale, 50 on Accelerate); very high-volume teams may need Enterprise, and contracts carry a 12-month minimum term after the trial window. Less positioned for live deal support. AutoRFP.ai is built around the questionnaire response workflow rather than real-time, in-call sales assistance, which is a different use case than SiftHub emphasizes. Uneven third-party review depth. Its review base is concentrated on G2 (56 reviews); Capterra shows only a single review, so cross-platform validation is limited. If AutoRFP.ai doesn’t look like a fit feel free to checkout our detailed blog on AutorRFP alternative AutoRFP.ai pricing Scale: $899/month paid annually, 24 projects per year, unlimited users and features Accelerate: $1,299/month paid annually, 50 projects per year. Enterprise: custom pricing that scales with project volume; per-project cost decreases as volume rises. Included on all tiers: SSO, 18+ integrations, unlimited support, onboarding, and a 30-day money-back guarantee. A "project" equals any single RFP, DDQ, tender, or security questionnaire. AutoRFP.ai ratings and reviews G2: 4.9 / 5 across 56 reviews. Capterra: 5.0 / 5 (1 review). Gartner Peer Insights: listed with a small number of high ratings; the vendor cites a 5.0 Gartner figure. Treat small samples cautiously. What are real users saying about AutoRFP.ai? Positive (G2): "Even on just one RFP process I saved myself over 6+ hours of manual worktime." verified G2 reviewer. [Review screenshot placeholder via G2] Mixed (G2): "Some of the UI is a little janky, and the import process can be slightly confusing for the most complex RFPs." verified G2 reviewer. Others add that web-only access is limiting and the initial learning curve is challenging. [Review screenshot placeholder via G2] SiftHub SiftHub , founded in 2023 by Manisha Raisinghani and backed by a $5.5M seed round (Matrix Partners India, Blume Ventures, and Neon Fund), positions itself as an "AI sales engineer" rather than a dedicated RFP tool. That framing matters for your evaluation: SiftHub is a broad deal-support platform, and RFP response is one module inside it alongside meeting prep, proposals, live in-call assistance, and ad hoc buyer questions. It acts as a central hub that collates and sifts content scattered across Drive, SharePoint, CRM, and knowledge bases. Solutions engineers and account executives use it to respond to RFPs, DDQs, and security questionnaires, build proposals, prepare for meetings, and answer ad hoc questions. Note: Because SiftHub is built as an AI sales engineer spanning the whole deal cycle, teams whose single, dominant need is high-volume RFP and questionnaire throughput should confirm the RFP module goes as deep as a purpose-built RFP platform during the demo. SiftHub best features High first-pass autofill across security formats. SiftHub reports auto-filling roughly 90% of responses on first pass across formats including SIG, VSAQ, CAIQ, and NIST 800-171, with each answer traced to a source. Pulse for live deal support. Pulse provides deal-aware, in-call assistance, surfacing answers in real time during conversations a capability aimed at presales rather than only document response. Live deal context. Answers can draw on live context from CRM and Gong, enabling buyer-specific personalization rather than documentation alone. Centralized search across repositories. It pulls content from scattered tools so users do not jump between systems, which reviewers cite as a core strength. Slack bot for instant answers. A Slack integration returns answers quickly inside the tools reps already use. Broad integrations and certifications. It connects to Slack, Salesforce, HubSpot, Drive, SharePoint, OneDrive, Notion, Gong, Zendesk, Teams, and Highspot, and reports ISO, SOC 2, and VAPT certification. SiftHub limitations Struggles on larger, complex documents. G2 reviewers note "limited features... especially when handling larger and complex documents," which can affect performance at scale. AI formatting issues. Reviewers mention formatting problems in AI output that require cleanup. Source transparency could improve. Some reviewers want stronger source transparency on generated answers. Generic answers needing manual tweaks. Reviewers note content is "sometimes... not fully aligned," feeling generic for industry- or customer-specific requirements and missing certain nuances. Buyers weighing this often read the dedicated Inventive SiftHub alternatives guide for a fuller side-by-side. Pricing is not published. SiftHub uses a custom quote model, so you cannot compare costs upfront without contacting sales. Shorter track record and smaller review base. Founded in 2023 with 22 G2 reviews, it has less long-term, at-scale validation than more established tools. Broad scope, RFP as one module. Because it spans multiple sales use cases, buyers focused purely on high-volume RFP throughput should verify the depth of the RFP module specifically. If Sifthub doesn't look like a fit feel free to checkout our detailed blog on Sifthub Alternatives . SiftHub pricing Model: custom quote only; no public rate card or published tiers. Variables: final cost depends on team size, volume, and integration requirements, per available third-party breakdowns. Recommendation: request a written quote that itemizes onboarding, integrations, and support so you can compare it like-for-like against AutoRFP.ai's published tiers. SiftHub ratings and reviews G2: 4.5 / 5 across 22 reviews. TrustRadius: a product profile exists; no numeric score was available at the time of writing. Gartner Peer Insights: listed; confirm current standing directly. What are real users saying about SiftHub? Positive (G2): reviewers say it "makes work on RFPs much easier and faster" with "accurate search that quickly pulls up past answers," helping teams stay consistent and avoid repeated work. [Review screenshot placeholder via G2] Mixed (G2): reviewers cite "limited features... especially when handling larger and complex documents" and answers that "feel generic" for industry-specific requirements, needing manual tweaking. [Review screenshot placeholder via G2] AutoRFP vs SiftHub: Feature-by-Feature Comparison AI Capabilities AutoRFP.ai: Drafts in your company's tone and terminology and attaches a Trust Score to each answer so reviewers can prioritize checks. SiftHub: Reports ~90% first-pass autofill across major questionnaire formats, with each answer traced to a source and drawing on live deal context. Note: Neither platform reliably prevents AI from generating answers outside the approved library, and neither publishes an independent hallucination benchmark. Verify source-grounding behavior directly during a demo with your own edge-case questions. On raw answer quality, the newer AI-native tools set a higher bar: Inventive AI cites a triple-blind, 100-question benchmark in which it produced 2x more client-ready answers than the next-best RFP AI tool it was tested against — the kind of side-by-side worth requesting from any vendor on your shortlist. Knowledge Management AutoRFP.ai: Centralized content library with a browser extension to work inside portals; content is imported from prior Word, Excel, and PDF responses. SiftHub: Acts as a hub that sifts content across Drive, SharePoint, CRM, and knowledge bases, reducing tool-switching. Workflow Automation AutoRFP.ai: Purpose-built bid workflows with SME assignment, reviewer stages, and real-time progress tracking. SiftHub: Bid/no-bid qualification, SME coordination, and governance workflows across the deal cycle. Integrations AutoRFP.ai SiftHub Stated count 18+ 11+ named CRM Yes (per vendor) Salesforce, HubSpot Content repositories Yes (per vendor) Drive, SharePoint, OneDrive, Notion, Highspot Communication Yes (per vendor) Slack, Teams Call intelligence Not emphasized Gong Confirm the specific connectors you rely on are live for your plan; integration availability can vary by tier. Security and Compliance AutoRFP.ai: ISO 27001:2022 certified and SOC 2 compliant, per its pricing and trust pages. SiftHub: Reports ISO, SOC 2, and VAPT (penetration-test) certification. Note: Both vendors publish security certifications, but certification scope and data-residency terms differ. Ask each for its current audit reports and where your data is stored. Analytics AutoRFP.ai: Emphasizes progress tracking and response efficiency; reviewers cite measurable time savings. SiftHub: Emphasizes deal context and usage across the sales cycle rather than published win-rate dashboards. Note: Neither vendor's public materials detail a deep, out-of-the-box win-rate analytics suite. If reporting is a priority, ask for a live look at the analytics screens. title: Checklist for Corporate and Sales Tax Compliance
summary: Small business tax compliance checklist covering federal returns, deadlines, payroll filings, and sales tax nexus by entity type. See what you owe and when.
body_text: Here’s what you need to know filing business taxes for 2024. A small business tax compliance checklist starts with your entity type, which decides the federal income tax return you file. From there it runs through estimated payments, payroll and information returns, state and franchise tax, and sales tax in every state where you have nexus. Here’s each piece, with the current filing season’s dates as the example. Match your entity type to the right federal return The IRS recognizes five business structures : sole proprietorship, partnership, corporation, S corporation, and LLC. Each maps to a specific federal return. Sole props and single-member LLCs report on Schedule C with Form 1040. Partnerships and multi-member LLCs file Form 1065. S corporations file Form 1120-S, and C corporations file Form 1120. Pass-through entities file first, so owners receive their Schedule K-1s in time to finish their personal returns. If you’re still choosing a structure, our guide to selecting a small business entity walks through the trade-offs. The table below lists the calendar-year deadlines, using this season’s 2026 dates as the example. Entity Form Original due date Extended date Partnership / multi-member LLC Form 1065 March 16, 2026 September 15, 2026 S corporation Form 1120-S March 16, 2026 September 15, 2026 C corporation Form 1120 April 15, 2026 October 15, 2026 Sole prop / single-member LLC Schedule C with Form 1040 April 15, 2026 October 15, 2026 Partnership and S corporation returns are due the 15th day of the 3rd month after year-end. When the 15th lands on a weekend, the deadline shifts to the next business day, which is how March 15 becomes Monday, March 16 in 2026. C corporation and Schedule C returns are due the 15th day of the 4th month, generally April 15. Estimated taxes and extensions Income tax isn’t only due once a year. Owners of pass-through entities pay quarterly estimated tax with Form 1040-ES. Per the IRS Form 1040-ES instructions , the four installments for a calendar year fall in April, June, and September, then the following January. C corporations owe estimated tax in four installments due the 15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months, figured on Form 1120-W and deposited through the Electronic Federal Tax Payment System (EFTPS). For the current season, the individual dates are April 15, June 15, and September 15, 2026, then January 15, 2027. Our breakdown of estimated tax timing covers the safe-harbor math. Need more time to file? Entities file Form 7004 for an automatic six-month extension, and individuals file Form 4868. An extension moves the filing date, not the payment date. Any tax owed is still due at the original deadline, and interest plus the failure-to-pay penalty accrue on the unpaid balance from that date. Our guide to business tax extensions explains when an extension helps and when it just delays the pain. Payroll and information returns If you have employees or pay contractors, a second calendar runs alongside your income tax return. According to the IRS employment tax due dates , Form 941 reports payroll tax each quarter and is due the last day of the month after the quarter ends. Form 940 reports annual FUTA and is due January 31. Forms W-2 and W-3 go to employees and the Social Security Administration by January 31, and Form 1099-NEC goes to contractors and the IRS by the same date. When January 31 falls on a weekend, these shift to the next business day. One threshold is changing. For tax year 2025 returns filed in early 2026, the old $600 Form 1099-NEC reporting threshold still applies. The IRS instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC confirm the One Big Beautiful Bill Act raised that threshold to $2,000 for payments made on or after January 1, 2026, with the first filings under the new rule due in January 2027. Track contractor payments against the threshold that applies to the year you’re filing, not the year you’re paying. State income and franchise tax State obligations sit on top of federal, and they don’t always track your income. Delaware corporations owe an annual franchise tax and must file the franchise tax report by March 1 each year. According to Wolters Kluwer , missing that date triggers a $200 penalty plus 1.5% monthly interest on the unpaid balance, and the report is filed through the Delaware Division of Corporations . This catches many owners who formed in Delaware but operate somewhere else. California charges an $800 minimum franchise tax on every LLC, corporation, and limited partnership registered in the state, owed regardless of income or activity, and generally due the 15th day of the 4th month. Nonpayment can lead to penalties, interest, and suspension of the entity’s rights. The takeaway is simple. Your state of formation, your state of operation, and every state where you have employees or property can each impose its own tax with its own form and its own date. Sales tax and economic nexus after Wayfair Sales tax is where a growing business quietly accumulates risk in states it has never set foot in. In South Dakota v. Wayfair, decided June 21, 2018, the Supreme Court let states require out-of-state sellers to collect sales tax based on economic activity alone. That is economic nexus. Per the Sales Tax Institute , South Dakota’s threshold is $100,000 in sales or 200 separate transactions into the state. Most states copied that model, but the outliers matter. California and Texas use $500,000 in sales with no transaction count, and New York requires $500,000 and more than 100 transactions, both together. All 45 states with a statewide sales tax, plus the District of Columbia, now have economic nexus rules. The trend is toward the dollar threshold alone. As of early 2026, 16 states have dropped the 200-transaction trigger, with Illinois removing it on January 1, 2026, and Kentucky on August 1, 2026. Physical nexus still counts on its own, so employees, an office, or inventory in a warehouse each create a collection duty. Marketplace facilitator laws make Amazon, eBay, and similar platforms collect on their own sales, but your website and trade-show sales stay your responsibility. The workflow is the same in every state. Determine where you have nexus, register for a sales tax permit, confirm which products are taxable, collect the correct combined state and local rate, then file and remit on the frequency the state assigns you. An annual sales tax check-up is the cleanest way to catch a new nexus line before it becomes a back-tax bill. That wasn’t so bad, was it? None of this is hard on its own. It gets hard at the seams. Bookkeeping that doesn’t match the return. A Delaware franchise notice nobody was watching. A sales tax registration that lapsed while revenue crossed a nexus line in three new states. A small business tax compliance checklist only works when one team owns every line of it, on a calendar, all year. That’s the case for keeping the whole checklist under one roof. Indinero bundles bookkeeping, accounting, and business tax into one monthly engagement, so the team that keeps your books is the team that files your return. The tax position always matches the financials it came from. Nothing gets handed across a gap. The other piece is breadth. Indinero serves the full range of entity types on this checklist, from sole proprietor and single-member LLC to multi-member LLC, S corporation, C corporation, and multi-entity structures. A business that starts as an LLC, elects S corp status, then converts to a C corp for a raise never has to switch providers or re-explain its history. The same engagement tracks federal deadlines, state and franchise tax, payroll filings, and multi-state sales tax nexus as you grow into new states. That continuity isn’t a given. With continuous operations since 2009, the same team stays on your books year after year, so your prior filings don’t disappear when a vendor changes hands. If you’d rather not run this alone, that’s what our business tax services and online bookkeeping teams are built for. Compliance shouldn’t feel like something you manage. It should feel like something that runs quietly in the background while you build the business. Frequently asked questions These are the questions small business owners ask most about staying tax-compliant. What should be on a small business tax compliance checklist? A small business tax compliance checklist has two halves, income tax and sales tax. Income tax means filing the right federal return for your entity type, making estimated payments, and completing payroll and information returns on time. Sales tax means registering and collecting wherever you have economic nexus. Indinero keeps both halves on one calendar, so nothing slips between the bookkeeping and the return. Which federal tax return does my business entity file? Your business entity type decides which federal return you file, from Schedule C for sole props to Form 1120 for C corporations. Partnerships file Form 1065, S corporations file Form 1120-S, and pass-through entities file first so owners receive their Schedule K-1s in time for personal returns. Indinero serves the full range of entity types, so a business that elects S corp status or converts to a C corp never has to switch providers. Does filing a tax extension give me more time to pay? No, a tax extension gives you more time to file, not more time to pay. Entities file Form 7004 and individuals file Form 4868 for an automatic six-month extension, but any tax owed is still due at the original deadline. Interest and the failure-to-pay penalty accrue on the unpaid balance from that date. Pairing bookkeeping and tax under one indinero engagement means your numbers are ready well before the payment is due. What is economic nexus and when do I have to collect sales tax? Economic nexus means a state can require you to collect sales tax based on your sales volume alone, even with no physical presence there. After South Dakota v. Wayfair in 2018, most states set a threshold near $100,000 in sales or 200 transactions, though California and Texas use $500,000. Indinero tracks multi-state nexus as you grow, so a new threshold gets caught before it becomes a back-tax bill. When are quarterly estimated taxes due for a small business? Quarterly estimated taxes for pass-through owners are generally due in April, June, and September, then the following January. Owners use Form 1040-ES, while C corporations figure estimates on Form 1120-W and deposit them through EFTPS on the 15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months. Missing an installment triggers underpayment penalties, so indinero maps these dates onto the same calendar that tracks your annual return. What changed with the 1099-NEC reporting threshold? The 1099-NEC reporting threshold rose from $600 to $2,000 for payments made on or after January 1, 2026. For tax year 2025 returns filed in early 2026, the old $600 threshold still applies under prior rules. The first $2,000 filings are due in January 2027. Because indinero keeps your books and your filings on one team, contractor totals are tracked against the correct year automatically.

title: Jake Pelligrini, Director of operations AIR, Athelas Commure
summary: Jake Pelligrini, Director of Operations at AIR, breaks down how the platform eliminates fragmented healthcare tech stacks, and why AI-powered chart notes and compliance tools are changing the game for PT clinics.
body_text: Transcript: My name is Jake Pelligrini. I'm the director of operations for AIR. and so my team focuses on getting clients onto Air. And I think there's a couple parts of that. Data migration training and change management, so the people side. There's the configuration side, and then new product features, trying to continue to push the envelope for what the product does. I think one of the things, really just around like a super seamless way for patients to schedule and get seen and get the care that they need. and really looking for all the different ways, all the different touch points that a patient has before they can come in, So trying to reduce any of the barriers like authorization or payments or anything like that such that a patient can walk in and get the care that they need quickly. The main for Air is really just that it's one platform. So there's different people who use the platform every day, but it all talks to each other and it all works together, seamlessly. So whether you're a front desk person scheduling patients or a clinician who is seeing patients or working on the billing side to make sure that those are those claims are paid, it all is one system that flows together. Versus trying to bolt together 15 different tech solutions and none of it talks to each other and none of it works well. I do think it's a fairly significant difference where we've built everything ourselves and so it is all kind of from the ground up versus trying to mash together a bunch of acquisitions that may or may not work together or may require three different logins even though it's quote unquote the same platform. I think with Air, the goal is that it's just you can focus on what actually matters in your job, you know, as opposed to needing to click through 15 different screens or, you know, have five different logins for different platforms that you're using. One of our strengths has been collaboration with our existing, partners. And so that means listening to them, iterating with them, building a prototype, getting their feedback, and really moving quickly. I think the state-of-the-art keeps moving fast, you know, AI, everything. But I think like how that really matters is just like can I do my job? Can I do my job better? Can I focus on the patient? Can I be more efficient? and so I think one of the things that I'm excited about is really just being able to push our product to an even greater spot, particularly with Rock Valley's scale and experience. and I think really just make sure that it's a seamless experience for everyone, an easy transition. you know, we work with people on training and getting them ready for the product and then that makes their day-to-day better as well. I think there's three things for Air. One is the scribe product, right? So that a clinician, a PT, can be talking to or or working with their patient and their chart note is filled out for them. I think the way that that can be customized to a site's needs to make sure that it's compliant, to meet, you know, to adjust to their preferences, I think is really something that does have that flexibility. Ease of use. It's intuitive. You can work with it right out of the box. It is really easy. It's intuitive. you know, simple colors, easy alerts. It tells you what you need to do and what actions you need to take. I think there's a lot of different opportunities for AI to be used in ways that actually make sense and drive value. So a simple example for that is just a compliance check. When you're done with your note, you can have a quick check for compliance and a grade for how well you did. I think the AI compliance chart note review is really something where you can look at it for a single note and then you can also see for the overall practice, how is the overall practice doing or how is a provider maybe taking feedback if they're a new student. You can see their score over time to see how they're doing, how they're filling out their chart notes. And so I think smaller parts where we use AI that makes sense or where we make an easy intuitive design really just make the end-to-end experience easy to learn system, easy to use system and it guides with like what the next step or what the next action is. It's a true partnership. It's, something that we're excited to push our product and build something with them and I think also drive value with the Rock Valley team so that we can all get to, you know, what is best-in-class and really really get like a a great experience for everyone. ‍

body_text: We are proud to share that Zoom was named a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Agentic Contact Center as a Service Platforms 2026 Vendor Assessment (doc #US54117326, August 2026). To us, this placement reflects the significant investment Zoom has made in building a contact center platform that is deeply integrated with AI, purpose-built on a unified communications foundation, and designed to meet the evolving expectations of both customers and the agents who serve them. See why Zoom was recognized Read excerpt What is the IDC MarketScape? The IDC MarketScape is an independent vendor assessment published by IDC. Zoom Contact Center was named a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Agentic Contact Center as a Service Platforms 2026 Vendor Assessment. We believe this position reflects Zoom's commitment to bringing trusted, AI-powered contact center capabilities to organizations of every size. Source: IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Agentic Contact Center as a Service Platforms 2026, Doc #US54117326, August 2026. Zoom's approach to contact center innovation Continuous improvement of autonomous behaviors, knowledge governance, and human-AI back-office collaboration. All three are fully supported and are within market expectations, reflecting a consistent emphasis on governed automation. Dedicated AI-focused R&D program. A well-documented, ongoing program advancing AI capabilities within the platform gives Zoom a credible, forward-looking innovation narrative. Strong workforce management foundation. Workforce management and quality assurance were among Zoom's strengths, reflecting robust capabilities in scheduling, coaching, and quality tools: a favorable signal for buyers prioritizing agent performance management. The momentum behind Zoom Contact Center Zoom's placement comes at a time of significant growth for Zoom's customer experience business . Zoom's own support team now resolves 97% of customer queries without a live agent using Zoom Virtual Agent, has increased CSAT by 28%, and saves 1,000+ agent hours per month . Customers like Vensure increased self-service rates from under 30% to trending toward 75% within just two months of deployment, and Cricut reduced call wait times by 89% and call abandonment rates by 90%. This momentum is connected to the value buyers are finding in Zoom's AI-first approach to contact center — particularly organizations that are ready to move beyond scripted bots and toward intelligent, adaptive virtual agents. Ready to see agentic AI in action? Watch the demo What this signals for organizations evaluating CCaaS If your organization is currently evaluating contact center platforms, Zoom's position as a Leader in the IDC MarketScape is worth considering in the context of your own priorities. Zoom Contact Center is a particularly compelling option for organizations already using Zoom Phone, Zoom Rooms, or Zoom Meetings. Extending a familiar interface into customer-facing operations can reduce training and change-management overhead. It is also a strong signal for buyers where AI-driven virtual agents are a primary purchase driver. Zoom's continued investment in agentic AI capabilities positions the platform well for organizations that want to move quickly in deploying autonomous customer experience technology. As with any significant platform decision, we encourage organizations with complex, large-scale enterprise contact center requirements to evaluate platform maturity and conduct thorough due diligence. The IDC MarketScape's assessment offers a structured, independent framework for doing exactly that. Zoom was also named a Visionary in the 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for CCaaS — a separate evaluation covering broader cloud contact center capabilities. Learn more about Zoom Contact Center If you're exploring what an AI-powered contact center could look like for your organization, we invite you to learn more about Zoom Contact Center and see how it can support your customer experience goals. Related Resources Zoom Contact Center product page Zoom Virtual Agent overview AI Expert Assist: how Zoom supports agents in real time Workforce Management in Zoom Contact Center Get the guide to getting started with contact center AI Get the guide Agentic contact center FAQs What is an agentic contact center? An agentic contact center is a customer service platform in which AI systems can autonomously reason, plan, and complete multi-step tasks — not just respond to a single prompt. Traditional contact centers rely on scripted, rule-based automation. Agentic AI goes further: it understands context, acts across connected systems, and resolves issues end-to-end. For a primer on what agentic AI means for your business, see Zoom's overview. In practice, this means a customer contacting support can have their issue understood, diagnosed, and resolved by an AI system that retrieves account data, processes a request, and confirms the outcome without requiring a live agent transfer for routine requests. Human agents remain in the loop for complex or sensitive situations, with AI handling oversight, guidance, and escalation routing throughout — and human supervisors maintaining visibility and control over AI behavior at all times. What is the difference between CCaaS and an agentic contact center? CCaaS — Contact Center as a Service — refers to cloud-delivered contact center infrastructure that provides routing, omnichannel support, workforce management, and analytics as a subscription service. Agentic contact centers build on that foundation by adding AI systems capable of autonomous actions like understanding customer intent and executing tasks. The shift from CCaaS to agentic contact center is less about replacing the platform and more about what the platform's AI layer can do. Zoom Contact Center is designed to support this evolution with Zoom Virtual Agent handling autonomous resolution, AI Expert Assist guiding live agents in real time, and Workforce Management tools enabling human oversight throughout interactions. How does Zoom Virtual Agent support agentic contact center use cases? Zoom Virtual Agent is Zoom's AI-powered virtual agent that can integrate with the Zoom Contact Center platform. It understands customer intent across text and voice channels, manages multi-step requests, executes tasks through integrations with CRM, ticketing, and back-office systems, and resolves issues without requiring a live agent transfer for routine requests. It is designed to handle the full resolution lifecycle rather than just collecting information. When escalation is needed, Zoom Virtual Agent passes the full context to the live agent so customers don't have to repeat themselves. Built-in QM and traceability means that contact center leaders can monitor AI behavior, review outcomes, and maintain governance over automated resolutions. What should CX leaders evaluate when choosing an agentic CCaaS platform? CX leaders evaluating enterprise contact center solutions should consider: how natively AI is built into the platform versus layered on top, whether the virtual agent can execute tasks or only gather information, how well the platform unifies self-service and live agent channels in a shared data layer, the depth of workforce management and quality assurance tooling, and how the vendor's innovation roadmap aligns with agentic AI capabilities. title: Astranis Launches Perceptor, Expanding into Space Domain Awareness and Maneuverability
body_text: Space is now a contested domain. Geosynchronous orbit and other high orbits have immense strategic value, and countries like China are building spacecraft capable of approaching, inspecting, and interfering with other nations' satellites. The infrastructure that connects, informs, and protects the world sits in an environment primed for conflict. Today, Astranis announced Perceptor, a new space domain awareness and maneuverability solution operating in GEO and other high orbits. Perceptor expands Astranis' offering beyond connectivity into a full-stack, multi-mission space infrastructure provider. Gaps in the current space environment will be used against the US and allies by those with ill intent. Proliferated GEO is the missing piece in our current capabilities. "Astranis provides mission-critical infrastructure for strategic higher orbits. What we found is our means to detect and respond to emerging threats to this infrastructure are sorely lacking," said John Gedmark, CEO and co-founder of Astranis. “There are blind spots that will be used against us if not eliminated. With Perceptor, we’re meeting the increasing demand for security in GEO with our proven on-orbit platform and ability to produce at scale.” ‍ ‍ Perceptor Capabilities: Observe and Inspect. An onboard sensor suite means the spacecraft can assess objects and activity in orbit. Multi-angle flybys can assess spacecraft capabilities, help troubleshoot anomalies on friendly spacecraft, and provide additional eyes in a domain where awareness has historically been limited. Maneuverability: Perceptor can both respond to nearby activity in real time, and use its electric propulsion system to traverse the full GEO arc, repositioning dozens of times over its mission lifetime. Swarm Tactics . Proliferated spacecraft mean new tactics to counter attempts at evasion, with an approach that scales to meet the needs of the mission. Speed. Perceptor uses Astranis’s flight proven MicroGEO platform and is ready to be produced at scale, built on the same production line as satellites that are flying today. Perceptor was designed for both commercial and national security missions in GEO and other high orbits. It's built on the same MicroGEO platform with five satellites already on orbit today, leveraging a proven approach to critical in-space infrastructure. ‍ About Astranis Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly-sophisticated customers across the globe – large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military. With five satellites on orbit and many more set to launch soon, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization. Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Blackrock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA. Astranis Media Contact Kati Dahm: press@astranis.com ‍

title: Willdan Expands Power Delivery Engineering Capabilities With KCS Corporation
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Willdan Group, Inc.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: ANAHEIM, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 17, 2026-- Willdan Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: WLDN) announced today that it has acquired substantially all of the assets of KCS Corporation (KCS), an engineering consulting firm headquartered in suburban Chicago, Illinois. KCS specializes in power delivery engineering for critical infrastructure. The 15-person KCS team expands Willdan’s in-house engineering and project management capabilities and adds capacity to Willdan’s APG team to support a growing pipeline of projects for data centers, battery storage, and grid modernization. "The demand for our energy infrastructure services has continued to grow,” said Mike Bieber, Willdan’s CEO. “In partnering with KCS on several substation and renewables projects, we recognized engineers and project managers who acted as a natural extension of our team. We’re pleased to welcome everyone at KCS to Willdan. Their addition further strengthens our in-house capabilities and allows our combined team to more efficiently execute on our power project pipeline and proactively meet this growing demand." “Building KCS Corporation has been an incredibly rewarding journey and we are proud of what we have accomplished together with our employees and clients,” said Seemesh M. Sethi, President of KCS. "We’re excited to join Willdan and for the opportunities this next chapter creates for continued growth of our business. We’ve worked closely with the APG team, now part of Willdan, and have experienced firsthand the strong alignment between our teams and how we serve clients. Bringing our capabilities together will allow us to offer our clients a broader range of engineering services while maintaining the personalized approach that has been central to KCS.” About KCS Corporation KCS Corporation is a diversified provider of engineering and construction support services with several years of experience in a variety of industries including telecommunications, power transmission and distribution, commercial and industrial automation, and renewable power generation. Since its founding in 1999, KCS has partnered with clients in the development and expansion of substations and transmission lines for investor-owned utilities. In addition, KCS has supported development of wind farms, utility scale solar, battery storage, generator backup power for data centers, and other essential facilities. About Willdan Willdan is a technical services company focused on energy and infrastructure solutions. These solutions include energy planning and analytics, consulting, software, public finance, engineering, and program implementation. Willdan serves utilities, state and local governments, and commercial customers in the United States and Canada. For additional information, visit Willdan's website at www.willdan.com or follow Willdan on LinkedIn and Facebook . title: BioNTech Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Corporate Update
body_text: Conference call and webcast scheduled for August 4, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. EDT (2:00 p.m. CEST) MAINZ, Germany, August 4, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- BioNTech SE (Nasdaq: BNTX, “BioNTech” or “the Company”) today reported financial results for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 and provided an update on its corporate progress. “In the first half of 2026, we made important progress in turning our mission into reality. We significantly advanced our late-stage oncology pipeline, with six pivotal trials initiated; we pioneered the generation of first-in-class global Phase 2 data for an investigational PD-L1xVEGF bispecific antibody in first-line non-small cell lung cancer across PD-L1 expression levels and histologies; and we demonstrated at medical congresses that our novel-novel combination therapy strategy is gaining momentum,” said Prof. Ugur Sahin, M.D., Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of BioNTech . “We look forward to welcoming BioNTech's next CEO. Guido Oelkers will take office by February 1, 2027, at the latest, and, together with the Management Board and teams across the company, is expected to continue to write the BioNTech success story.” Financial Review for Second Quarter and First Half of 2026 in millions €, except per share data Second Quarter 2026 Second Quarter 2025 IFRS Results Adjusted Results2 IFRS Results Adjusted Results2 Revenues 105.60 105.60 260.80 260.80 Net loss (820.80) (562.30) (386.60) (348.80) Diluted loss per share (3.24) (2.22) (1.60) (1.45) in millions €, except per share data Year-to-date 2026 Year-to-date 2025 IFRS Results Adjusted Results2 IFRS Results Adjusted Results2 Revenues 223.7 223.7 443.6 443.6 Net loss (1,352.7) (1,056.9) (802.4) (779.6) Diluted loss per share (5.34) (4.17) (3.33) (3.23) Below figures compare the second quarter of 2026 and the year-to-date period ended June 30, 2026, to the corresponding prior year periods, except as noted. Revenues were €105.6 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared to €260.8 million. Year-to-date revenues were €223.7 million, compared to €443.6 million. The decreases in both quarterly and year-to-date revenues compared to the prior year were primarily driven by lower demand from BioNTech’s COVID-19 vaccines. Research and development (“R&D”) expenses were €551.0 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared to €509.1 million. Year-to-date R&D expenses were €1,108.0 million, compared to €1,034.7 million. R&D expenses were mainly driven by higher expenses for the development of immuno-oncology (“IO”) and antibody-drug conjugate (“ADC”) programs, in particular pumitamig and gotistobart, impairment losses of intangible assets, and the inclusion of operations from CureVac, which was acquired in late 2025. The quarterly and year-to-date increases were partially offset by lower costs from non-focus programs and positive effects from cost shares with BioNTech’s collaboration partners. Adjusted R&D expenses were €477.1 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared to €509.1 million. Year-to-date adjusted R&D expenses were €1,004.2 million, compared to €1,034.7 million. Adjusted R&D expenses for both the second quarter and year-to-date period in 2026 exclude impairment losses of intangible assets. Sales, general and administrative (“SG&A”) expenses were €197.8 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared to €137.4 million. Year-to-date SG&A expenses were €348.6 million, compared to €258.0 million. The increases in both quarterly and year-to-date were mainly driven by the ongoing pre‑launch activities and commercial build-up, the inclusion of operations from CureVac, and expenses associated with BioNTech’s global initiative on scaling processes and ERP infrastructure to strengthen operational execution. This was partly offset by cost reductions resulting from the execution of initiatives related to BioNTech’s pipeline prioritization and increased cost discipline. Other operating result was negative €207.9 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared to negative €39.0 million. Year-to-date other operating result was negative €224.3 million, compared to negative €25.9 million. Both quarterly and year-to-date decreases were primarily driven by higher expenses in connection with BioNTech’s pipeline prioritization. Adjusted other operating result was negative €23.3 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared to negative €1.2 million. Year-to-date adjusted other operating result was negative €32.3 million, compared to negative €3.1 million. Adjusted other operating results for both the second quarter and year-to-date periods in 2026 and 2025 exclude employee-related costs and impairment losses, both related to BioNTech’s pipeline prioritization. Net loss was €820.8 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared to a net loss of €386.6 million. Year-to-date net loss was €1,352.7 million, compared to a net loss of €802.4 million. Adjusted net loss was €562.3 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared to an adjusted net loss of €348.8 million. Year-to-date adjusted net loss was €1,056.9 million, compared to an adjusted net loss of €779.6 million. Diluted loss per share was €3.24 for the second quarter of 2026, compared to a diluted loss per share of €1.60. Year-to-date diluted loss per share was €5.34, compared to a diluted loss per share of €3.33. Adjusted diluted loss per share was €2.22 for the second quarter of 2026, compared to an adjusted diluted loss per share of €1.45. Year-to-date adjusted diluted loss per share was €4.17, compared to adjusted diluted loss per share of €3.23. Cash, cash equivalents and security investments as of June 30, 2026 were €16,634.2 million, comprising €9,741.0 million in cash and cash equivalents, €5,035.1 million in current security investments disclosed as financial assets and €1,858.1 million in non-current security investments disclosed as financial assets. Shares outstanding as of June 30, 2026 were 251,204,366, excluding 7,823,121 shares held in treasury. In May 2026, BioNTech entered into a share repurchase program , pursuant to which the Company may purchase American Depositary Shares (“ADSs”), each representing one ordinary share of the Company, in the amount of up to $1.0 billion until and including May 6, 2027. During the second quarter of 2026, 1,693,056 ADSs were repurchased at an average price of $89.50 (€77.85), for total consideration of $151.6 million (€131.8 milion). “We are revising our full-year 2026 financial guidance in light of recently emerged external developments,” said Ramón Zapata, Chief Financial Officer at BioNTech . “Our capital allocation strategy is delivering results: our financial position is strong, our share repurchase program is well underway, and we continue to make meaningful progress across our pipeline. Moving forward, we continue to execute on our strategy to turn BioNTech into a multi-product biopharmaceutical company by 2030.” Revised 2026 Financial Year Guidance5: 2026 FY Guidance (March 2026) 2026 FY Guidance (August 2026) Revenues €2,000 – €2,300 million €1,600 – €1,900 million BioNTech is revising its full-year 2026 financial guidance revenue range due to: COVID-19 vaccine market Softer than anticipated global COVID-19 vaccine demand In Germany existing vaccine inventory will be used in the 2026 vaccination season The timing of milestone-related revenues resulting from an out-licensed R&D program, which are no longer expected in 2026. BioNTech continues to expect the majority of 2026 revenues to be realized in the second half of the year, specifically in the third quarter, when it also expects to recognize the €613 million Bristol Myers Squibb Company (“BMS”) collaboration revenue. Planned 2026 Financial Year Adjusted Expenses5: 2026 FY Guidance (March 2026) 2026 FY Guidance (August 2026) Adjusted R&D expenses €2,200 – €2,500 million €2,000 – €2,300 million Adjusted SG&A expenses3 €700 – €800 million €700 – €800 million BioNTech now expects adjusted R&D expenses in the range of €2.0 billion to €2.3 billion. Adjusted SG&A expenses remain unchanged in the range of €700 million to €800 million. This reflects BioNTech’s focus on optimizing its R&D resources and continued cost discipline as it prioritizes the development of its late-stage clinical pipeline. The Company expects these cost savings based on prioritization and optimization to continue into future years. BioNTech's strong balance sheet and continued cost discipline support the Company's ability to invest strategically. Corporate and Commercial Update for the Second Quarter 2026 and Post Period Events On August 3, 2026, BioNTech announced that the Supervisory Board has appointed Guido Oelkers, Ph.D., to the Management Board as Chief Executive Officer (“CEO”), who will take office by February 1, 2027, at the latest, succeeding Prof. Ugur Sahin, M.D. Guido Oelkers is a seasoned CEO and strategic leader with over 30 years of experience in the biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries. He has a strong track record of transforming and scaling global organizations, driving sustainable growth through disciplined execution, focused capital allocation, and operational excellence. Throughout his career, Guido Oelkers has successfully built, prioritized and strengthened complex and innovative product portfolios across multiple areas, including oncology and immunology, while driving global business operations in key markets, notably in the United States. He will join BioNTech from the global Nasdaq Stockholm-listed biopharmaceutical company Swedish Orphan Biovitrum AB (“Sobi”), where he has served as CEO since 2017. In May 2026, the Company held its Annual General Meeting (“AGM”). Shareholders approved expanding the Supervisory Board from six to eight members and adding additional expertise: Prof. Iris Löw-Friedrich, M.D., Ph.D., and Susanne Schaffert, Ph.D., were elected as new members of the Supervisory Board. Variant-adapted COVID-19 Vaccine BioNTech and Pfizer Inc. (“Pfizer”) have submitted regulatory applications to the European Medicines Agency (“EMA”) and to the United States Food and Drug Administration (“FDA”) for approval of their XFG variant-adapted monovalent COVID-19 vaccine for the 2026-2027 vaccination season. In July 2026, BioNTech and Pfizer’s XFG variant-adapted monovalent COVID-19 vaccine was approved by the European Commission following recommendation for marketing authorization by the EMA’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (“CHMP”). Select Oncology Pipeline Updates Next-Generation Immunomodulators and Combinations Pumitamig (BNT327/BMS986545) is an investigational bispecific immunomodulator combining PD-L16 checkpoint inhibition with VEGF-A neutralization that is being developed in collaboration with BMS. Pumitamig is currently being evaluated in seven pivotal trials across the ROSETTA clinical development program, with five new global clinical trials initiated in the first half of 2026 spanning triple-negative breast cancer, colorectal cancer, gastric cancer, and non-small cell lung cancer, including two NSCLC clinical trials in patients with unresectable stage III disease and advanced PD-L1 ≥ 50% disease, respectively. A global Phase 2/3 clinical trial (ROSETTA Lung-02; NCT06712316 ) is ongoing to evaluate pumitamig in combination with chemotherapy compared to pembrolizumab and chemotherapy in patients with first-line NSCLC. The Phase 3 part of the trial is currently recruiting. In May 2026, data from the Phase 2 part of the trial was presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology (“ASCO”) Annual Meeting 2026. The data showed encouraging anti-tumor activity, with high response rates observed in both non-squamous and squamous NSCLC and across PD-L1 expression levels. Pumitamig is also being evaluated in additional solid tumor indications, including first-line hepatocellular carcinoma (“HCC”), second-line glioblastoma (“GBM”), first-line pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (“PDAC”) and first-line renal cell carcinoma (“RCC”) in various Phase 1/2 and Phase 2 trials, both as monotherapy and in combination with standard of care. BioNTech has several signal-seeking clinical trials ongoing evaluating pumitamig in novel/novel combinations with the Company’s proprietary assets. These trials will inform the dose selection for pumitamig and explore anti-tumor activity in multiple tumors for later-stage development. Multiple data readouts from these combinations are expected in 2026. Gotistobart (BNT316/ONC-392) is a tumor microenvironment-selective regulatory T cell depletion candidate that targets CTLA-4 and is being developed in collaboration with OncoC4, Inc. (“OncoC4”). A global Phase 3 clinical trial (PRESERVE-003; NCT05671510 ) is ongoing to evaluate the efficacy and safety of gotistobart as monotherapy in patients with metastatic squamous NSCLC that progressed on previous platinum-based chemotherapy and PD-(L)1-inhibitor treatment. In March 2026, updated data from the non-pivotal dose-confirmation stage, the first of two stages of the global Phase 3 clinical trial, were presented at the European Lung Cancer Congress (“ELCC”). Gotistobart demonstrated a clinically meaningful overall survival benefit (hazard ratio: 0.46) compared to standard of care chemotherapy and a manageable safety profile in patients with squamous NSCLC whose disease had progressed following anti-PD-(L)1 therapy and platinum-based chemotherapy. Updated data from the Stage 1 of this trial are expected to be presented at the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (“IASLC”) 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer (“WCLC”). Based on current event accrual projections, the first interim analysis from Stage 2 of the two-stage Phase 3 clinical trial is expected in 2026. A Phase 2 clinical trial (PRESERVE-004; NCT05446298 ) is being conducted to evaluate gotistobart in combination with pembrolizumab in patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (“PROC”). In May 2026, data from the trial were presented at the ASCO Annual Meeting 2026. Gotistobart in combination with pembrolizumab demonstrated encouraging and durable antitumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with PROC. Antibody-Drug Conjugates Trastuzumab pamirtecan (BNT323/DB-1303) is an ADC candidate targeting HER2 that is being developed in collaboration with Duality Biologics (Suzhou) Co. Ltd. (“DualityBio”). A Phase 1/2 clinical trial ( NCT05150691 ) is being conducted to evaluate trastuzumab pamirtecan in patients with advanced HER2-expressing tumors. A potentially registrational cohort with HER2-expressing (IHC3+, 2+, 1+ or ISH-positive) patients with recurrent endometrial cancer (“EC”) is fully recruited. In June 2026, additional data were presented from the Phase 2 portion of the trial at the ESMO Gynaecological Cancers Congress 2026 in Copenhagen, Denmark. Trastuzumab pamirtecan showed encouraging and durable anti-tumor activity and meaningful survival in patients with advanced HER2-expressing endometrial cancer. The safety profile was manageable and consistent with the known class effects of anti-HER2 ADCs. A Phase 3 clinical trial (FERN-EC-01, NCT06340568 ) is being conducted to evaluate trastuzumab pamirtecan compared to investigator’s choice of chemotherapy in patients with advanced and HER2-expressing recurrent EC. A Phase 3 clinical trial (DYNASTY-Breast02, NCT06018337 ) to evaluate trastuzumab pamirtecan in patients with HR-positive, HER2-low metastatic breast cancer is ongoing. Based on current event accrual projections, the primary analysis is expected in the fourth quarter 2026. While BioNTech and DualityBio plan to file a biologics license application (“BLA”) in 2026, the companies will determine the optimal regulatory path for trastuzumab pamirtecan based on the totality of clinical data in endometrial cancer and breast cancer. This approach is in line with the companies’ value-optimization strategy for the asset in an evolving treatment landscape and focuses on prioritizing opportunities where they can deliver significant benefit for patients. Elfetabart drozuntecan (BNT324/DB-1311) is an ADC candidate targeting B7-H3 that is being developed in collaboration with DualityBio. More than one thousand patients have now been treated with elfetabart drozuntecan in clinical trials across more than ten tumor types, including 400 patients treated with elfetabart drozuntecan in combination with pumitamig. In May 2026, a Phase 3 clinical trial ( NCT07365995 ) to evaluate elfetabart drozuntecan compared to docetaxel in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (“mCRPC”) was initiated.
